Remittances and school enrolment in rural Bangladesh

ABSTRACT

Remittances can relax budget constraints that keep children out of school. Using a panel of 3,000 households, we find remittances raise secondary enrolment for girls by 9 percentage points but have no effect for boys.

KEYWORDS: remittances; education

1. Introduction

Migration is rising.

6. Conclusion

Remittances close part of the gender gap in secondary schooling in rural Bangladesh.

Policies that lower remittance costs may have education benefits.
